data.title: Kestra Financial Taps BlackRock Veteran to Head Wealth Management — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

Kestra Financial has recruited a BlackRock executive to head its wealth management operations. Kelly Apple joined Kestra July 6. Kestra announced the move on Wednesday.

Apple will oversee the broad portfolio of services Kestra offers its financial advisors, including retirement planning, insurance, and alternative investments. Her title will be head of wealth management, and that role will cover both Kestra Financial and Kestra Private Wealth Services, the company's channel for breakaway advisors.

"Advisors today are being asked to deliver increasingly comprehensive advice across every stage of a client's financial life," Apple says. "Kestra has built something unique in this industry-a strong foundation for advisors who want to grow and deepen their client relationships-and I'm excited to help expand the capabilities and resources that support their success."

Apple succeeds John Amore as head of wealth management. Kestra Financial announced the promotion of Amore to president in January, and he assumed that role in April.

Since that transition, Kestra has been considering how its wealth management leadership can better support its advisors, who cater to wealthy clients.

"When I stepped into the role of president, our leadership team saw an opportunity to thoughtfully define what this position needed to be for the future of our business," Amore says. "Kelly's experience building partnerships and high-performing teams, paired with a deep understanding of what today's advisors need to grow, will help our community of complete wealth managers thrive."

Apple comes to Kestra after a 13-year stint at BlackRock, where she most recently served as managing director and head of national accounts, overseeing the firm's largest distribution arrangements. She first registered as a broker with Van Kampen Funds in 2003, according to registration records. She joined DWS Investments Distributors in 2010 before jumping to BlackRock in 2012.

BlackRock declined to comment on her departure.

data.title: CUKTECH Introduces Intelligent Cooling and Fast-Charging Solutions for Modern Lifestyle
data.description:
KUALA LUMPUR, MY / ACCESS Newswire / August 21, 2026 / CUKTECH has unveiled three new lifestyle devices designed for consumers to stay cool, connected and powered throughout their day. The new line-up comprises the CUKTECH CP Turbo Fan Plus, CUKTECH 6 Ultra Charger and CUKTECH 10 Ultra Charger, each combining high-performance technology with practical features designed for work, travel and daily use.

"Consumers today expect technology to work seamlessly alongside their lifestyles," said a representative of CUKTECH. "Whether they are commuting, travelling, working remotely or spending time outdoors, they want products that deliver performance without adding complexity. The CP Turbo Fan Plus, 6 Ultra Charger and 10 Ultra Charger were designed to provide greater comfort, convenience, and flexibility wherever users go."

CUKTECH CP Turbo Fan Plus

Designed specifically for Malaysia's hot and humid weather, the CUKTECH CP Turbo Fan Plus delivers powerful portable cooling through a next-generation three-phase brushless motor capable of operating at speeds of up to 30,000 revolutions per minute (rpm). The fan generates wind speeds of up to 11 meters per second, providing strong airflow that helps users stay comfortable in outdoor and indoor environments.

Users can choose from three standard airflow settings according to their cooling needs, while an additional BOOST mode provides an instant burst of high-speed airflow for more demanding situations. Malaysia's hot and humid weather can make even short periods outdoors uncomfortable, particularly during the afternoon. Whether walking between an LRT or MRT station and the office, waiting outdoors for an e-hailing ride, or spending time at an open-air event, the CP Turbo Fan Plus provides portable airflow that can be easily carried throughout the day.

One of the product's key innovations is its modular magnetic design, which enables the fan unit and battery module to be attached or detached according to user preference. The detachable battery module houses a 10,000mAh battery, capable of delivering up to 37 hours of operating time, depending on usage conditions and airflow settings.

Beyond powering the fan, the battery module also functions as a portable power bank. Its USB-C port supports up to 27W input and 33W output, while the Power-Pin Magnetic interface supports up to 25W output. The fan can also continue operating while charging, ensuring uninterrupted cooling during extended periods of use. Additional features include an anti-hair-entanglement grille for safer usage, intuitive dual-button controls, a three-colour battery indicator and a durable nylon carrying strap that enhances portability.

CUKTECH 6 Ultra Charger

For consumers seeking a more efficient charging solution, the CUKTECH 6 Ultra Charger delivers up to 100W of charging output through two USB-C ports and one USB-A port. The charger is capable of simultaneously powering a wide range of compatible devices, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, earbuds and other personal electronics.

Built using advanced GaN (gallium nitride) technology, the charger combines high charging performance with a compact form factor, making it particularly suitable for travellers, professionals and users who frequently carry multiple devices. With laptops, smartphones and earbuds now part of the everyday work or study setup, access to enough charging points can become an issue when working from a café, shared workspace or while travelling. The 6 Ultra Charger consolidates these charging needs into a single compact device, with three ports allowing multiple devices to be powered from one wall socket.

Its intelligent power allocation system automatically adjusts charging output according to the needs of connected devices, improving charging efficiency while optimising power delivery. The device is further enhanced by a 0.96-inch high-definition smart display, which provides real-time charging information such as total power output, voltage, current and individual port performance. The display can be rotated by 180 degrees, ensuring easy viewing regardless of socket orientation. Supported by OPC 2.0 Smart Charging technology and broad charging protocol compatibility, the 6 Ultra Charger is designed to work seamlessly across major device ecosystems, including compatible products from Apple, Xiaomi, Samsung and Huawei.

CUKTECH 10 Ultra Charger

Completing the new line-up is the CUKTECH 10 Ultra Charger, a premium high-performance charger developed for users who regularly manage multiple devices at the same time. Delivering up to 120W of total charging output, the charger features three USB-C ports and one USB-A port, allowing laptops, tablets, smartphones and other electronic accessories to be powered from a single device.

Its intelligent dynamic power allocation technology automatically distributes charging output according to the number and type of connected devices, helping users achieve optimal charging efficiency while reducing the need to carry multiple chargers. At the centre of the device is a 1.57-inch TFT smart display that provides real-time charging information, including power output, voltage, current and operating temperature. The charger also supports Bluetooth connectivity and integration with the Mi Home application, enabling users to monitor charging performance and manage supported settings from their smartphones.

Despite offering four charging ports and high output capabilities, the 10 Ultra Charger retains a compact and travel-friendly design, weighing approximately 239g, making it suitable for workstations, travel setups and multi-device households. For professionals who rely on a laptop throughout the workday while keeping a phone, tablet or other accessories powered at the same time, the 10 Ultra Charger supports laptop fast charging of up to 100W alongside a broader multi-device setup. Its 1.57-inch display and Mi Home integration also allow charging performance to be viewed and managed more easily, whether used at a workstation or packed for a business trip.

In conjunction with the launch, the CUKTECH CP Turbo Fan Plus will retail at RM199 with a special launch price of RM193, while the CUKTECH 6 Ultra Charger and CUKTECH 10 Ultra Charger will be available at RM149 and RM189 with a special launch price of RM145 and RM183 respectively. The special launch prices will be available for one month from the official launch date.

Malaysian consumers can also discover the latest products and learn more about their features through CUKTECH's Shopee Live session and official Shopee store in Malaysia, where the new line-up will be available for purchase upon launch.

To learn more about CUKTECH and its latest products, visit https://cuktech.com/ or follow CUKTECH on Facebook and Instagram. Consumers can also join CUKTECH's Malaysia and Asia community pages for the latest product updates, promotions and announcements.

###

ABOUT NANJING CUKTECH ELECTRONICS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. ("CUKTECH")

CUKTECH is a technology-driven innovative company, dedicated to creating a comprehensive clean energy ecosystem for its users. Since its journey began in 2016, CUKTECH has achieved remarkable milestones in the charging market, including developing popular charging products for Xiaomi that have garnered praise from both media and users. Today, CUKTECH products are sold across vast countries and regions worldwide. With a steadfast commitment to product innovation, over 51.4% of our team focuses on research and development, ensuring meticulous attention to detail and delivering products that users love. Known for its commitment to creating a comprehensive clean energy ecosystem, CUKTECH offers a range of cutting-edge products now available on Shopee and Lazada.

data.title: Yields extend rise following strong US services data
data.description:
Key points:
  • S&P Global flash services PMI rises to 56.8 in August from 54.6 in July
  • Two-year Treasury yield up 3.8 basis points to 4.223%
  • Thirty-year Treasury yield rises 3 basis points to 5.266%

By Colin Barr

U.S. Treasury yields rose modestly on Friday, on track to end an eventful week with another round of selling after data showed a strong expansion this month in the U.S. services sector.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2YT=RR) was up 3.8 basis points at 4.223% in early trading and the 10-year yield was up 2.6 basis points at 4.724%.

The yield on the 30-year long bond (US30YT=RR), where the week's major dramas largely played out, was up 3 basis points to 5.266%, putting it below the decade-plus highs it reached this week but above the levels following Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's surprise buyback announcement on Wednesday and his jawboning a day later.

The strongest growth in the U.S. services sector in nearly two years powered a sharp acceleration in overall business activity in August, offsetting a slowdown in the manufacturing sector, which was restrained by reduced stock building and supply disruptions from the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

S&P Global said on Friday its flash services Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.8, the highest level since December 2024, from 54.6 in July. That jump drove its Composite Output Index up to 56.0, the highest reading since April 2022, from 54.5 last month.

Those PMI surveys suggest that nearly two-thirds of the way through the current third quarter, overall U.S. economic growth is on track to double the second quarter's 1.5% annualized expansion rate. The strong performance will add to concerns about gathering U.S. economic momentum pushing price levels higher at a time when investors are increasingly worried about the fiscal outlook and the prospect that inflation will remain elevated.

Earlier on Friday, the S&P Global Eurozone Manufacturing PMI rose to a 54-month high and employment increased for the first time in three years.

SENTIMENT IN U.S. MARKETS REMAINS MOSTLY BULLISH

There is little major economic data on the slate in the coming week, beyond the release of U.S. GDP and Personal Consumption Expenditures data early on Wednesday and Nvidia earnings that evening. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is expected to deliver the keynote speech next Friday morning at the U.S. central bank's annual Jackson Hole conference in Wyoming.

Analysts, as a result, were left to size up the vibes in a market that has been anxious about the prospect of significantly higher rates yet also resilient in the face of pullbacks.

"Taking a step back, deficit concerns have once again become a focal point of the macro narrative, helping underpin the bearishness in the Treasury market," said Ian Lyngen, head of U.S. rates strategy at BMO Capital Markets.

Lyngen noted that the cumulative U.S. budget deficit for fiscal year 2026 is the highest since 2021, the national debt surpassed $40 trillion this week and long-term borrowing costs are pushing federal interest payments on the debt higher.

"It's with this backdrop that 30-year yields are trading at the highest levels since the GFC (Global Financial Crisis), despite Bessent's remark that, 'There's nothing magic about the 40-trillion number. We can grow our way out of that.'"

Sentiment in U.S. markets, however, remains mostly bullish. U.S. equities indexes took a hit on Thursday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling more than 1%. But the decline left the blue-chip index just 3% below its August 5 record close and about 3.6% below its record intraday high, which was also reached that day. It was up 0.6% early on Friday.

"We're all too cognizant that dramatic and unanticipated moves have a tendency to occur in the late-summer trading period," Lyngen said. "It's with a wary eye that we'll be on headline watch this August Friday as the weekend can't get here soon enough."

data.description:
Automakers around the globe have issued a wave of recalls over the years to fix defects ranging from faulty cameras and infotainment systems to airbags, ignition switches and, more recently, software-related snarls.

Eleven carmakers, including Tesla and Xiaomi , launched software updates and vehicle recalls on Friday, adding to a growing list of automakers caught up in China's largest-ever automotive recall campaign, to remedy their emergency door-release systems.

data.title: Crypto Stocks Gain as Bitcoin Heads for Best Week in Over Two Years — WSJ
data.description:
By Vicky Ge Huang

Crypto stocks are rising Friday as bitcoin is headed for its best weekly performance in more than two years.

Shares of Coinbase Global, the largest crypto exchange in the U.S., were up 10% Friday morning. Robinhood Markets jumped 13%. Strategy, the bitcoin accumulation firm led by Michael Saylor, gained 8%.

Bitcoin recently traded around $77,500 after spiking to $79,426 earlier in the day. It has been climbing since the Treasury Department announced its expanded bond buyback program, which continues to weigh on the dollar.

The largest cryptocurrency is still well below its previous peak above $126,000 in October, but its sudden move upward has lifted other digital currencies and crypto-linked stocks.

Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, has advanced about 27% this week and is on pace for its best week in more than five years. It recently traded around $2,400.

Analysts attribute bitcoin's recent surge to institutional demand and market dynamics. More than $1 billion has flowed into exchange-traded funds tracking the cryptocurrency in the past two days, while billions of dollars in bearish positions were liquidated over the past week, creating a short squeeze that propelled the token's price higher.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: British Economy Has Held Up Well Against Iran War, PM Switch — Market Talk
data.description: The further rise in U.K. PMIs and consumer confidence at its highest level in two years suggests households and businesses have taken the Iran war and government change of administration remarkably well, RSM U.K.'s Thomas Pugh says. "If we're not careful, we might have to stop talking about resilience and actually start talking about a reasonable economic performance this year," he says in a note. The second half looks more challenging, with oil prices rising again and inflation set to climb to 3.5%. The government's budget announcement has the potential to make or break the final quarter, Pugh says. "A repeat of the confidence-sapping speculation about tax rises will cause growth to slow sharply. However, the economy is clearly holding up so far this year." (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

data.title: Hugoton: Trustee says no cash distribution for August as excess costs suspend payouts
data.description:
The trustee of Hugoton announced there will be no cash distribution for May 2026 due to excess cost positions across the Trust’s Kansas, Oklahoma and Wyoming conveyances, and the Trust’s cash reserve was reduced by $8,000 for expenses. Accumulated excess costs and low commodity prices have resulted in no unitholder distributions since July 2023 and raise substantial doubt about the Trust’s ability to continue as a going concern. The trustee is reviewing options including potential termination or sale of the Trust’s net profits interests, and the Trust has ceased seeking a new auditor and suspended SEC reporting due to cash constraints.

Financial Highlights

  • No cash distribution declared for May 2026; Trustee reduced the cash reserve by $8,000 to pay Trust expenses.
  • Accumulated excess costs have produced no unitholder distributions since July 2023, contributing to a depleted expense reserve.
  • Underlying cumulative excess costs — Kansas: $3,289,000 (including $405,000 interest); Oklahoma: $15,058,000 (including $1,387,000 interest); Wyoming: $12,735,000 (including $1,585,000 interest).
  • Advance distributions of $1,000,000 (net to the Trust) from XTO Energy are recoupable and may be applied as production cost recoupment subject to a $250,000 minimum available cash covenant.
  • Trust unable to engage a new independent registered public accounting firm and filed a Form 12b-25; SEC reporting and audited financial statements are currently suspended due to cash constraints.

Business Highlights

  • Trust revenues for the current month are driven by net overriding royalty receipts from gas and oil produced primarily in May; recorded underlying sales volumes were ~693,000 Mcf gas and ~13,000 bbls oil for the current month.
  • Reported average realized prices for the referenced month were $2.80/Mcf for gas and $100.73/bbl for oil (prior month: $3.06/Mcf gas, $93.52/bbl oil).
  • Mach Natural Resources reported development costs of $1,471,000, production expense of $1,414,000 and overhead of $904,000 used in the royalty calculation for the current month.
  • Trustee has curtailed discretionary spending, including deferral of the Trustee fee since April 2024, and has engaged potential third parties about interest in the Trust’s net profits interests though no offers have resulted.

Original SEC Filing: HUGOTON ROYALTY TRUST [ HGTXU ] - 8-K - Aug. 21, 2026
